title: The pluperfect: what had already happened

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the pluperfect (*había* + past participle) from B1 Unit 1. It says that something had already happened before another moment in the past. In this lesson that moment is the export boom or a census: *Antes del auge, muchas familias habían trabajado tierras pequeñas.*

items.spanish: Antes del auge exportador, muchas familias habían trabajado tierras pequeñas.
items.english: Before the export boom, many families had worked small plots of land.

items.spanish: Según el censo de 1914, alrededor del treinta por ciento de la población había nacido en el extranjero.
items.english: According to the 1914 census, about thirty per cent of the population had been born abroad.

items.spanish: Muchos inmigrantes habían llegado sin tierra y trabajaban en la cosecha del trigo.
items.english: Many immigrants had arrived without land and worked in the wheat harvest.

sections.content: Use *había* / *habían* only for the earlier event; tell the main story in the preterite or the imperfect. The participle never changes: *habían llegado*, not *habían llegados*.
